title: Fran Beresford (she/they)
text:
I am currently finishing my Phd in the Networks, Computational Analysis and Social Dynamics Lab led by Professor Butts at the University of California, Irvine.
I am on the job market and am excited to move onto the next stage of my career as a postdoctoral researcher - my interests are environmental statistics and health policy. I work primarily with Bayesian methods on network data but I have also worked with remote sensing data. In an ML context I have used random features to estimate non-parametric coefficients for Exponential Family Random Graph Models.
I am originally from the UK (northern England) and have also lived in Barcelona, Spain as an au-pair before starting graduate school.
I have worked as a statistician for the UK Civil Service full time in two different positions, in the Department for Health and Social Care and the Department for Work and Pensions.
A big part of my life during my student career has been involvement with the graduate student government / student social clubs. At my undergraduate institution I was the social coordinator for the student Maths society as well as a volunteer during Welcome Week. In graduate school I sat on the graduate school council for 4 years and held both paid and unpaid positions for the UCI Associated Graduate Students.

title: About me
text:
In summary:

My love of statistics was born when I was informed I didn’t have a choice in taking a class for my Maths A-Level in the UK, which I then continued with to gain an entire A-Level in Statistics. (A-Levels are qualifications one completes during the ages of 16-18 in the UK.)
I completed my MMath Degree, an integrated Masters degree with a year-long working placement, at the University of Bath, UK. There I won the James Duthie Award upon graduation, which is awarded to an outstanding graduate of the maths department. I gained my degree with First Class Honours.

After spending 3 months as an au pair in Barcelona and a further 6 months working for the UK Department for Work and Pensions I was ready to move to California to start the next chapter.
I started my PhD at the University of California Irvine in September of 2020 and I will be defending my thesis in the next few months.
